children: Gold’s three-month correlation with the S&P 500 has climbed to 0.35, indicating the two assets tend to move in the same direction. The correlation has doubled since February and stayed positive throughout 2026, unlike in 2025, when it was negative for most months, according to BeInCrypto.

Gold is down about 18% so far in 2026 and is on track for its biggest annual decline since 2013, when it fell 28%, The Kobeissi Letter noted. On Friday, a selloff in gold and silver pushed gold to its lowest level in more than a year as stocks fell in the U.S. and Asia. Gold had peaked in late January. The decline marks a break from a pattern dating to 1974, when gold rose in every year U.S. stocks lost 10% or more; that streak ended in 2022, when gold slipped slightly as stocks tumbled.

The article attributes much of gold’s weakness this year to the bond market: inflation-protected Treasuries are paying close to 3% above inflation, raising the cost of holding gold, while bets on further Fed hikes have weighed on equities as part of a broader rates shock. The Kobeissi Letter said gold is on track for its biggest annual drop since 2013, when investors sold bullion for stocks, which finished near six-year highs. Its data also show the correlation swung from strongly positive to deeply negative during 2025. BloFin’s outlook sees room for gold to recover after another Fed hike if real yields fall; until then, it says a working hedge would mean gold holding steady on days stocks fall.

title: Gold’s Correlation With S&P 500 Climbs to 0.35 as Both Assets Move Together
